title: SGIP: Learning Scene-Grounded Interaction Priors for Scene-Aware Human Motion Prediction
claim: Prior methods rely on ambiguous distance or gaze cues; ours predicts an explicit grounded target distribution that conditions accurate prediction without extra sensing.
layout: 2 sections, left-to-right; dashed divider, arrows linking (b) stages, bar chart
description: The figure has two groups. Panel (a), 'Previous Methods', shows a 3D-scanned room with a yellow human figure. Purple dotted arrows give distances (1.72m, 1.43m) and a gaze cone, with the caption that geometry is ambiguous and gaze needs extra sensing. Panel (b), 'Ours (SGIP)', has three stages joined by black arrows. First, 'Ambiguous future grounding' shows colored trajectories from the person to the bag, sofa, chair and free space, with a 'Where to go?' inset view below. Second, 'Explicit Interaction Prior' shows the same room with colored dotted regions and a bar chart of probabilities for Bag 1, Bag 2, Sofa, Chair and Free Space, with the sofa highest at 0.32. Third, 'Scene-Grounded Prediction' shows blue human pose sequences walking to and sitting on the sofa. Color-coded tokens z1 to z5 link each region to its bar. Bold captions sit under each stage.
caption: Overview of the proposed method. Scene-aware human motion prediction (HMP) requires resolving future-motion ambiguity. (a) Previous methods handle this ambiguity implicitly, relying on motion--scene distance or gaze without an explicit interaction target; geometry alone is ambiguous when several objects lie at similar distances, and gaze requires extra sensing. (b) Given the same observed motion, a person may approach a bag, sit on the sofa or chair, or freely navigate the room. SGIP resolves this by predicting an explicit scene-grounded interaction prior, a distribution over candidate scene tokens covering both object instances and free space, from the observed motion and 3D scene alone. Distilled at training time from an intent-aware teacher that combines semantic and geometric scores, the prior places the highest probability on the sofa token, which conditions both trajectory and full-body pose prediction to correctly anticipate walking toward and sitting on the sofa, with no extra sensing at inference.
abstract: Human motion prediction (HMP) aims to forecast future movement from an observed motion sequence, and recent methods have incorporated 3D scene geometry and object semantics to improve long-term plausibility. However, the destination of future motion remains ambiguous in cluttered scenes: the same observed motion can lead to different interaction targets or navigation modes. Existing methods either handle this ambiguity implicitly or rely on auxiliary signals like gaze that are hard to obtain in practice. To address this, we propose SGIP, which explicitly predicts where in the scene future motion will be grounded across both objects and open navigation regions, and uses it to condition future trajectory and full-body pose prediction. This scene-grounded interaction prior is learned via intent distillation: at training time only, a teacher model scores candidate scene regions by combining an LLM prompted with a textual description of the person's intent with geometric motion-scene features. A student model learns to reproduce these scores from only the observed motion and 3D scene, making intent and LLM unnecessary at test time. Across multiple benchmark datasets, SGIP outperforms prior scene-aware baselines on both trajectory and pose accuracy in a realistic deployment setting where neither gaze nor intent is available at inference, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The project page is available at https://sgip2026.github.io.
